_meta.note: The source strings, and the key set translators work from. English also lives in the HTML as the fallback, so this file is never fetched at runtime — a missing key renders the English already on the page.
_meta.englishOnlyReason: Legal and evidential wording: the INEC disclaimer and the non-affiliation notice. A mistranslated disclaimer is a legal exposure. These stay in English until a human translator signs for them.

about.an-independent-nonpartisan-record-: An independent, nonpartisan record of what was announced at each polling unit — documented, verified and published by ordinary Nigerians.
about.elections-are-won-at-the-polling: Elections are won at the polling unit, then at collation. When numbers can change on the way up, trust collapses. So every report here is photographed, signed on the observer's own phone and chained on a public ledger — and a count is trusted only when independent observers at the same place agree, backed by GPS and matching venue photos.
about.hawkeye-does-not-declare-winners-a: Hawkeye does not declare winners, and its tallies are not official results — those come only from INEC. It is a record built to aid scrutiny, unaffiliated with INEC, any party, candidate or campaign.

faq.anyone-with-a-nigerian-mobile-number: Anyone with a Nigerian mobile number and a phone with a camera and GPS. Verify your number once, then report from the polling unit where you observe the count. No accreditation, membership or payment needed.
faq.can-a-report-be-edited-or: Can a report be edited or deleted afterwards?
faq.can-one-person-submit-multiple-repor: Can one person submit multiple reports with different SIM cards?
faq.each-device-carries-a-fingerprint-an: Each device carries a fingerprint, and one device can report each race only once — no matter how many numbers are registered on it. Independent reports must come from genuinely different people on different phones.
faq.how-do-i-get-alerts-for: How do I get alerts for races I care about?
faq.how-is-my-verification-code-sent: How is my verification code sent?
faq.is-hawkeye-official-are-these-the: Is Hawkeye official? Are these the real election results?
faq.it-is-hashed-one-way-scrambled: It is hashed (one-way scrambled) before storage and is never published or shared. It exists solely so one number equals one observer.
faq.map-your-unit-before-election-day: map your unit before election day
faq.my-polling-unit-doesn-t-appear: My polling unit doesn't appear near me. Why?
faq.no-gallery-uploads-ever-both-photos: No gallery uploads, ever. Both photos — the EC8A results sheet and the venue — are captured in-app and GPS-stamped on the spot. This is what makes a Hawkeye report hard to fake from somewhere else.
faq.no-hawkeye-is-an-independent-communi: No. Hawkeye is an independent, community-run transparency initiative. The tallies shown here are crowd-verified evidence of what was announced at individual polling units — the official results of any election are only those declared by INEC.
faq.tap-any-question-to-expand-it: Tap any question to expand it.
faq.what-happens-to-my-phone-number: What happens to my phone number?
faq.when-independent-observers-at-the-sa: When independent observers at the same unit submit matching counts — backed by GPS, matching venue photos and automatic reading of the sheet. Until then a count stays visibly marked as reported or provisional.
faq.why-must-photos-be-taken-live: Why must photos be taken live? Can I upload from my gallery?
faq.your-one-time-code-arrives-free: Your one-time code arrives free of charge on the channel you choose at sign-up — Telegram or WhatsApp. Open the link shown there, confirm your contact (it must match the number you typed), and the code arrives instantly. Race alerts reach you in the app's notifications feed, and on Telegram.
guide.everything-you-need-to-do-before: Everything you need to do — before, during and after the count at your polling unit.
guide.geofenced-units-only-accept-report: Geofenced units only accept reports from people standing there.
guide.good-light-no-glare-no-fingers: Good light, no glare, no fingers over the figures column.
guide.hard-rules-the-app-enforces-these: Hard rules — the app enforces these
guide.if-the-app-warns-the-photo: If the app warns the photo is blurry or washed out, retake it.
guide.live-photos-only-no-gallery-upload: Live photos only; no gallery uploads, no screenshots.
guide.one-report-per-election-per-pollin: One report per election per polling unit per observer — and one per election per device, regardless of how many SIMs it holds.
guide.open-the-report-page-once-on: Open the report page once on Wi-Fi so it saves to your phone, grant camera and location permission, and charge enough to last through the evening count.
guide.point-the-camera-at-the-whole: Point the camera at the whole sheet — the scanner outlines it and captures automatically when steady.
guide.reports-are-permanent-nothing-can-: Reports are permanent. Nothing can be edited or deleted after signing.
guide.take-a-separate-photo-of-the: Take a separate photo of the polling unit — the building, banner or surroundings. This lets the system confirm different observers stood at the same place.
guide.the-rules-that-keep-reports-honest: The Rules That Keep Reports Honest
guide.type-each-party-s-announced-figure: Type each party's announced figure exactly, then sign and submit while still at the unit. Photos expire if you wait, and your GPS must match where the photos were taken. Several elections may be counted at your unit the same day — submit one report per election, each with its own photos.
guide.voting-ends-then-the-presiding-off: Voting ends, then the presiding officer counts ballots publicly and fills in the EC8A result sheet for each election. This — the announcement — is the moment that matters.
how.a-ledger-nobody-can-quietly-edit: ⛓️ A ledger nobody can quietly edit
how.a-verified-phone-number-is-one: A verified phone number is one observer identity. Numbers are stored only as one-way hashes — never readable, never published.
how.each-photo-is-gps-stamped-at: Each photo is GPS-stamped at capture; the sheet, venue and submission positions must all agree, and photos expire within minutes.
how.each-report-is-signed-on-the: Each report is signed on the observer's phone with a key that never leaves it, then chained to the previous entry by cryptographic hash.
how.each-report-is-tagged-to-its: Each report is tagged to its races automatically — state, senatorial district and federal constituency come from the official register.
how.every-unit-also-has-an-approximate: Every unit also has an approximate area from open geographic data; reports or mapping fixes far outside it are rejected outright.
how.hawkeye-turns-thousands-of-ordinary-: Hawkeye turns thousands of ordinary phones into a network of independent witnesses. No single report is trusted on its own — trust is earned when separate people, provably at the same place, say the same thing.
how.map-your-unit-before-election-day: Map Your Unit Before Election Day
how.most-polling-units-have-no-verified: Most polling units have no verified GPS location. Stand at yours and pin it before the vote.
how.photos-are-captured-live-in-the: Photos are captured live in the app — the EC8A sheet is auto-detected, flattened and quality-checked (blur/glare) like a document scanner.
how.re-submitting-someone-else-s-photo: Re-submitting someone else's photo — or a near-identical copy — is detected and rejected by image fingerprinting.
how.tap-each-layer-to-see-how: Tap each layer to see how it works.
how.the-typed-counts-are-cross-checked: The typed counts are cross-checked against the digits machine-read from the sheet photograph itself.
how.units-without-one-accept-reports-but: Units without one accept reports, but the count stays visibly "location-unverified" until at least three independent observers' GPS positions cluster at the same spot.
how.venue-photos-from-different-observer: Venue photos from different observers are feature-matched to confirm they stood at the same physical place.
how.verify-your-phone-then-photograph-th: Verify your phone, then photograph the announced EC8A results sheet and the venue on election day. Your report is signed on your device and recorded permanently.
how.watch-the-leaderboard-live-and-subsc: Watch the leaderboard live, and subscribe to alerts for the presidential race, your state, senatorial district or constituency.

integrity.automated-flags-aid-scrutiny-t: Automated flags aid scrutiny; they are not proof of fraud. Official results remain INEC's.

ledger.the-chain-head-can-be-anchored: The chain head can be anchored on a public blockchain, so not even the server operator can rewrite history unnoticed. Official results remain INEC's.

osun.candidate-information-is-compiled-f: Candidate information is compiled from public declarations and INEC's published list, and may lag announcements. Hawkeye is nonpartisan and does not endorse any candidate. Official candidate lists and results are INEC's.
political.grouped-by-geopolitical-zone-o: Grouped by geopolitical zone — open one to see its states.
political.incumbency-data-is-provisional: Incumbency data is provisional and community-maintained; verify against INEC. Official results remain INEC's.
practice.nicely-done-that-s-exactly-how: Nicely done — that’s exactly how you report a result on election day.
practice.on-election-day-you-take-two: On election day you take two live photos here — the results sheet and the venue. Try it now (or tap “Use a sample” if you’d rather skip the camera in practice).
practice.on-election-day-your-report-is: On election day your report is signed on your phone and added to the public, tamper-evident ledger. Here it just completes the practice.
practice.type-the-number-of-votes-each: Type the number of votes each party was announced to have at the unit.
preview.mock-data-random-winners-for-lay: MOCK DATA — random winners, for layout preview only. On election day each state fills with the leading party's official emblem as reports arrive.
privacy.all-traffic-is-encrypted-https-p: All traffic is encrypted (HTTPS). Phone numbers are HMAC-hashed, reports are signed on your own device with a key that never leaves it, and access is rate-limited and bot-screened.
privacy.hawkeye-is-built-to-protect-the: Hawkeye is built to protect the people who use it. This explains exactly what we collect, why, what becomes public, and what stays private.
privacy.one-time-codes-they-expire-in: One-time codes — they expire in minutes and are deleted on use.
privacy.sell-rent-or-share-your-data: Sell, rent or share your data.
privacy.use-tracking-cookies-only-a-sign: Use tracking cookies — only a sign-in token and your keys, kept on your device.
privacy.your-actual-number-only-the-hash: Your actual number — only the hash exists.
privacy.your-identity-no-report-is-linke: Your identity — no report is linked to your name or number.
profile.deletes-your-observer-identity-y: Deletes your observer identity: your key, device link, Telegram link and subscriptions are wiped. Reports already on the public ledger are permanent and stay; re-registering the same phone restores the same ID.
profile.this-is-the-unit-you-ll: This is the unit you'll get alerts about. You don't need to be there now.
profile.your-public-identity-on-the-ledg: Your public identity on the ledger — your phone number is never stored.
race.candidate-information-is-compiled-f: Candidate information is compiled from public declarations and INEC's published lists, and may lag announcements. Hawkeye is nonpartisan and does not endorse any candidate. Official candidate lists and results are INEC's.
results.charts-appear-as-soon-as-reports: Charts appear as soon as reports arrive.
results.filter-the-leaderboard-by-state-: Filter the leaderboard by state or district
results.party-emblems-are-used-for-ident: Party emblems are used for identification only. Auto-refreshes every 30 seconds.
results.unopened-races-can-be-viewed-the: Unopened races can be viewed — they simply have no results yet.
support.always-confirm-the-address-after: Always confirm the address after pasting. Hawkeye will never message you asking for funds or seed phrases.
support.hawkeye-is-built-and-paid-for: Hawkeye is built and paid for by its founder — no political funding, no advertisers, no strings attached. If the work is useful to you, a donation helps cover the servers, phones and time that keep it running and independent.
terms.do-not-attempt-to-disrupt-overload: Do not attempt to disrupt, overload, reverse-engineer, or gain unauthorised access to the service.
terms.do-not-upload-unlawful-defamatory-: Do not upload unlawful, defamatory, or harassing content, or media you have no right to share.
terms.hawkeye-is-a-free-independent-nonp: Hawkeye is a free, independent, nonpartisan election-transparency tool. By using the website, mobile app, or any Hawkeye service, you agree to these terms. Last updated 13 July 2026.
terms.hawkeye-is-provided-as-is-without: Hawkeye is provided “as is”, without warranties of any kind. Crowd-reported data is partial and unofficial and may contain errors; it is offered for transparency and scrutiny, not as a definitive count. We do not guarantee uninterrupted or error-free service.
terms.hawkeye-may-publish-its-own-public: Hawkeye may publish its own public-service content (for example, election-integrity explainers and result summaries) to its official accounts on third-party platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook, using those platforms' official APIs. Such posts are made only from Hawkeye's own accounts and are subject to the respective platform's terms. Hawkeye does not access, collect, or post to any third-party user's social-media account.
terms.never-put-yourself-at-risk-to: Never put yourself at risk to gather a report. Follow all applicable laws.
terms.official-election-results-are-thos: Official election results are those declared by INEC alone.
terms.one-verified-phone-number-is-one: One verified phone number is one observer identity. Do not attempt to create multiple identities, evade anti-fraud controls, or file duplicate or automated reports.
terms.submit-only-truthful-reports-of-wh: Submit only truthful reports of what you genuinely witnessed at a polling unit. Do not fabricate, alter, or misrepresent results, photos, or locations.
terms.to-the-maximum-extent-permitted-by: To the maximum extent permitted by law, Hawkeye and its operators are not liable for any indirect, incidental, or consequential damages arising from your use of, or inability to use, the service, or from reliance on any crowd-reported data.

faq.no-every-report-is-signed-on-the: No. Every report is signed on the observer's device and chained onto a public, tamper-evident ledger. Anyone can re-verify the whole chain on the Verify the Ledger page. If a report is wrong, the remedy is more independent reports — matching counts from separate observers outweigh a bad one.
faq.most-of-nigeria-s-176-846-polling: Most of Nigeria's 176,846 polling units have no published GPS location. You can still report — find your unit through the register browser (state → LGA → ward). Better still, map your unit before election day so it is geofenced on the day.
faq.verify-your-phone-once-then-on-the: Verify your phone once, then on the results page choose an election and a state, district or constituency and press Follow. You'll get an alert — in the app, and on Telegram — whenever new reports land.
guide.on-the-report-page-enter-your-nige: On the report page, enter your Nigerian mobile number and confirm the one-time code sent to you on Telegram or WhatsApp. Do this days ahead — not in the queue.
guide.visit-your-unit-open-map-a-polling: Visit your unit, open Map a Polling Unit, and capture its GPS position while standing there. Once a few people do this, the unit is geofenced for election day — only people actually there can report it.
guide.7-enter-the-counts-and-submit-imme: 7 Enter the counts and submit immediately
guide.gps-too-weak-step-into-open-sky: GPS too weak — step into open sky, away from roofing, and retry.
guide.no-code-arrived-resend-it-from-the: No code arrived — resend it from the report page, switching between Telegram and WhatsApp if needed; the number must match the one you typed.
guide.photos-too-old-retake-both-photos-: "Photos too old" — retake both photos and submit straight away.
guide.session-expired-verify-your-phone-: Session expired — verify your phone again; your identity and history are preserved.
how.photograph-the-evidence-two-live-pho: Photograph the evidence. Two live photos — the EC8A results sheet and the venue — each GPS-stamped the moment it is taken. Gallery uploads are impossible.
how.sign-on-your-device-the-counts-photo: Sign on your device. The counts, photo fingerprints and location are signed with a key that never leaves your phone, then chained onto a public ledger. Nothing can be edited or quietly deleted afterwards.
how.independent-agreement-a-count-is-onl: Independent agreement. A count is only marked verified when separate observers at the same unit report matching numbers — backed by GPS, matching venue photos, and the digits read from the sheet itself.
how.every-phone-also-carries-a-device-fi: Every phone also carries a device fingerprint. One device can report each race once, no matter how many SIM cards or accounts it holds.
how.units-with-a-confirmed-location-are-: Units with a confirmed location are geofenced: reports are only accepted from people standing there.
how.before-election-day-volunteers-crowd: Before election day, volunteers crowd-map units the same way — three agreeing fixes confirm a unit's location in advance.
how.changing-or-removing-any-past-entry-: Changing or removing any past entry breaks the chain publicly. Anyone can re-verify it in their browser on the Verify the Ledger page.
how.matching-counts-from-independent-obs: Matching counts from independent observers push a unit's confidence up; conflicting counts mark it disputed — visibly, never silently resolved.
how.the-leaderboard-rolls-verified-units: The leaderboard rolls verified units up per race, with grey regions still awaiting reports.
how.follow-any-race-everywhere-or-a-sing: Follow any race — everywhere, or a single state, district or constituency — and Hawkeye pings you — in the app, and on Telegram — whenever new reports land. Subscribe on the results page.
how.what-hawkeye-is-not-hawkeye-does-not: What Hawkeye is not: Hawkeye does not declare winners and its tallies are not official results. It is a public, independent evidence record of what was announced at polling units. Official results are those declared by INEC.

info.why-collation-forms-matter.title: Why collation forms matter
info.why-collation-forms-matter.body: Collation happens at three levels: ward (EC8B), LGA (EC8C) and state (EC8D). Hawkeye checks each form's totals against the polling-unit sheets underneath it, so a party's number that shrinks on the way up is flagged publicly — that gap between the units and the declared total is where a count is most often changed.
info.what-happens-to-this-report.title: What happens to this report
info.what-happens-to-this-report.body: Your report is signed on this device and written to the public tamper-evident ledger, so it cannot be edited or withdrawn afterwards. It is checked against the polling-unit evidence in this area, and its fingerprint is published to the public Rekor transparency log in the next daily anchor.
info.how-the-docket-works.title: How the docket works
info.how-the-docket-works.body:
A flag never decides anything — it holds that unit's votes out of every tally until the crowd clears them.

Why a disputed result is excluded — until the crowd reviews a flag, the unit's votes stay out of every tally. Holding a possibly-bad result while it is checked is safer than letting it inflate a total; nothing is deleted, only set aside until it is cleared or struck.

Who judges, and how — verified observers worldwide, never Hawkeye. Each answers factual questions about the evidence on file: the results-sheet photo, the venue photo, the GPS fix. No one at Hawkeye casts a verdict.

The docket is on the chain — every case, verdict and resolution is appended to the docket's own tamper-evident chain, anchored to a public transparency log. The jury is as auditable as the count itself.
info.what-appears-here.title: What appears here
info.what-appears-here.body: Violence, vote-buying, BVAS failures, obstruction and more, filed by observers at the scene. Every report shown on this page was reviewed by a human before it was published — reports still under review are not listed.
info.what-to-report-and-what-happens-nex: What to report, and what happens next

Violence, ballot snatching, vote-buying, voter intimidation, BVAS failure, late materials, obstruction — anything that affected the vote. A person reviews every report before it appears; approved ones are published in the feed below, identified by observer ID only.
info.what-gets-checked.title: What gets checked
info.what-gets-checked.body: Over-voting, impossible turnout, forged form serials, conflicting counts and statistical outliers. A flag is a signal for scrutiny, not a verdict — and never proof of fraud.
info.digit-distribution-screening.title: Digit-distribution screening
info.digit-distribution-screening.body: Fabricated figures cluster on favourite digits, while genuine counts follow known distributions — Benford's law for first digits, and a roughly even spread for last digits. A departure means these numbers are worth a closer look, nothing more. Real elections throw up odd-looking distributions for innocent reasons, so a flag here is a prompt to check the evidence, not a finding of fraud.
info.inec-irev-cross-check.title: INEC IReV cross-check
info.inec-irev-cross-check.body: For each polling unit, the crowd's reported count is compared against the EC8A sheet INEC itself uploads to its Results Viewing portal (IReV) — INEC's own evidence checked against the crowd's, neither one trusted over the other. Any mismatch appears in the discrepancies above, with a link straight to INEC's sheet so you can look yourself.
info.collation-reconciliation.title: Collation reconciliation
info.collation-reconciliation.body: Ward (EC8B), LGA (EC8C) and state (EC8D) collation totals are checked against the polling-unit sheets they are built from. A collated figure can never be LESS than the sum of the covered units alone — when it is, that is arithmetic proof of subtraction, not a matter of opinion, and it is flagged in the discrepancies above. This is the step where a count is most often changed.
info.how-the-chain-is-checked.title: How the chain is checked
info.how-the-chain-is-checked.body: Each entry stores the hash of the one before it, so altering or removing any past report breaks every hash after it. This page recomputes the whole chain in your own browser and compares the head it gets to the one we publish — you don't have to trust us.
info.verifying-a-single-race.title: Verifying a single race
info.verifying-a-single-race.body: Every anchor batches every race — Presidential, and each Senate, House, Governorship and State Assembly race — into one Merkle root published to Rekor. Verifying one race folds only that race's branch, in your own browser, without replaying every other race or trusting us.
info.reading-this-page.title: Reading this page
info.reading-this-page.body: Each state is coloured by its governing party. Tap or hover a state for its governor, party and the year of its next election. Figures are compiled from public records and updated as results are declared.
info.where-these-numbers-come-from.title: Where these numbers come from
info.how-races-are-grouped.title: How races are grouped
info.how-races-are-grouped.body: Ongoing is an election being reported today. Upcoming is one whose polling day is still ahead. Completed is one whose polling day has passed — its page stays up, because the record is the point. Candidate lists appear on each race's page as INEC publishes them, roughly 28 days out.

info.why-mapping-units-matters.body: Most polling units have no confirmed location on record, so results reported from them cannot be location-checked. When a few independent people map the same unit, its location is confirmed and every result filed there on election day can be matched against it.

terms.what-hawkeye-is-body: Hawkeye lets citizens photograph, sign, and publish the results announced at their polling unit to an independent, tamper-evident public record. Hawkeye is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or acting on behalf of INEC, any government body, or any political party. Official election results are those declared by INEC alone. Hawkeye produces crowd-reported evidence for public scrutiny; it does not, and cannot, declare a winner.
terms.your-content-body: Reports you submit — counts, photos, and their locations — are published on a public, tamper-evident ledger and, by design, cannot be edited or deleted; that permanence is what makes them trustworthy. By submitting, you grant Hawkeye a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free licence to store, publish, and display that content for election-transparency purposes. You confirm you have the right to submit it. Your phone number is never published — see the Privacy Policy.
terms.changes-contact-body: We may update these terms; continued use after changes constitutes acceptance. Questions: info@hawkeye.com.ng. Governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.
privacy.collect.number: Your number — as a hash. One-way, never reversible. We cannot see it, show it, or hand it over; it exists so one number equals one observer.
privacy.collect.reports: Your reports — the counts, two live photos, and where each was taken.
privacy.collect.device: A device fingerprint — hashed, so one phone cannot report the same race twice.
privacy.collect.telegram: Your Telegram link — the chat ID only, so the bot can reach you. We never read your messages or contacts.
privacy.what-becomes-public-body: Your counts, photos and their locations go on a public ledger and cannot be edited or deleted — that permanence is what makes them worth anything. They are tied to an anonymous observer ID, never to you. Incident media appears only after human review.
privacy.your-rights-body: You can delete your account yourself at any time: open your profile and choose Delete my account. This removes your signing key, device link, Telegram link and alert subscriptions. Two things remain, by design: public ledger entries (permanent and anonymous — that permanence is what makes them trustworthy) and the one-way hash of your number, kept so a deleted identity can't be reused to file duplicate reports. Re-registering the same number restores your original observer ID. Other Nigeria Data Protection Act requests: info@hawkeye.com.ng.
notifications.alerts-are-kept-for-90-day: Alerts are kept for 90 days. Reports, incidents and the ledger are permanent.
